mechanism: On each published conditioning clock for a pair's own economy, the proposal reads the market's INITIAL reaction direction and holds in that direction: the reaction R is the log return of the pair's daily 16:00-NY decision-close series from the last pre-availability decision close close(D_prev) to the first post-availability decision close close(D0); direction = sign(R); the position is filled at the NEXT decision close (no same-bar fill) and held k decision sessions with a unconditional time exit. The slow actor is the sticky-information agent (Mankiw & Reis 2002) and the slowly-rebalancing institutional allocator: Coibion & Gorodnichenko (2015) measure that forecasters underreact to macro news, so the consensus expectation path catches up to a CPI print over days, and each forecast revision maps into a same-direction order flow; the fast actor is forced short-horizon flow (stop/option hedging, market-maker inventory cover) that sets the first post-release close. The effect should exist because the first post-availability decision close is set under time pressure at wide spreads while the inattentive cohort completes incorporation only over the following sessions: that is the post-announcement-drift shape (Ball & Brown 1968; Bernard & Thomas 1990) transplanted to FX, where Andersen, Bollerslev, Diebold & Vega (2003, 2007) document both large announcement jumps and economically significant post-announcement persistence, and where UIP failure around prints (Fama 1984) implies rate-surprise news is not fully impounded at the announcement close. No print VALUES and no consensus estimates are used or assumed: the DIRECTION signal is the pair's own measured price reaction, computable from staged price series plus the evidenced availability stamps alone; reaction-magnitude is reported as a diagnostic but never gates a trade (zero-threshold design).

information_source.calendars: research/control/forex_free_v6_run/p3_conditioning_clocks_v6.json (246 clocks: GB 88 / CA 105 / AU 23 / NZ 30; each clock carries available_time_utc + precision + archive_sha256; CA v3 TRUE-UTC semantics per P0b; S0 2018-04-04..2025-07-24 frozen)
information_source.prices: staged daily snapshots under data_raw/forex_free_v1 (156-file manifest-verified, manifest sha256 fe2155c0ef51bcac32262ebaf1c7d98fc724727eca1dda8b6644012ad854c460, INHERITED_BYTE_VERIFIED per p2_data_authority_v6.json); the 4h snapshots are NOT used by this proposal (daily-or-slower only)
information_source.direction_computation: R = ln(close(D0)/close(D_prev)) on the pair's daily decision-close series; direction = sign(R); R computed to float precision; R == 0 exactly -> event skipped and counted zero_signal_skipped; |R| reported as diagnostic only, never a gate
information_source.warmup: 5 decision closes of the pair's decision series must exist ending at close(D_prev); an event without full warmup is skipped fail-closed and counted warmup_skipped (first S0 clocks are 2018-04-18 GB / 2018-04-19 NZ / 2018-04-20 CA, so this binds only against staging edge, not the S0 window)
information_source.print_values_or_consensus: NOT USED and NOT ASSUMED - see open_feasibility_questions_for_A9

conditionability_rule.CA_INSTANT: all 105 CA clocks carry available_for_daily_decision_date; conditionable at the 16:00-NY decision on that published date. For the 102 scheduled 08:30-Toronto rows it equals the release date (12:30Z stamp precedes the 20:00Z/21:00Z decision instant); for the 3 published boundary_shift rows (2018-05-28 -> 2018-05-29, 2018-05-29 -> 2018-05-30, 2021-07-23 -> 2021-07-26) the print is conditionable ONLY at the published next-weekday available_for_daily_decision_date
conditionability_rule.GB_AU_DAY: DAY-precision clocks (23:59:59Z end-of-day bound, ONS Release date field / ABS Released field) are conditionable at the 16:00-NY decision on their published decision_date, per the published convention 'available for the daily decision on its decision_date by construction'
conditionability_rule.NZ_INSTANT: INSTANT Stats NZ PublicationDate stamps under the published flat +12:00 conservative-LATER convention are conditionable at the 16:00-NY decision on decision_date (expressed instants precede that decision for all 30 published rows)
conditionability_rule.fail_closed_rule: any clock whose published stamp contradicts these semantics at implementation time is skipped and reported; clocks NOT published in p3_conditioning_clocks_v6.json (AU pre-Sep-2019 quarterlies, AU mid-2022 gaps, all non-funded economies) are never conditionable - no inferred availability, per P-1
conditionability_rule.reaction_window_definition: D0 = first conditionable decision date; D_prev = immediately preceding weekday decision date; reaction window = [close(D_prev), close(D0)]; for the 3 CA boundary rows D_prev is the release-date decision close, which precedes the after-16:00-NY release instant, so the window captures the overnight-plus-next-day reaction by construction

clock: daily 16:00 America/New_York (zoneinfo DST-correct); daily-or-slower only; no intraday decisions; signals computed at decision closes, fills at decision closes

features: clock economy, decision_date, available_time_utc, archive_sha256 (attribution features)
features_lags.lags: R uses closes lagged at most 1 decision session (close(D_prev)); no other lags; no rolling windows; no thresholds

entry_exit_fill_rules.signal_decision_instant: 16:00-NY decision on D0, using data through close(D0)
entry_exit_fill_rules.entry_fill: close(D1) where D1 = next weekday after D0 (FX 24/5 weekday convention, no holiday refinement - published next_trading_day_rule); FILL AT NEXT DECISION CLOSE, never same-bar
entry_exit_fill_rules.hold: k decision sessions (anchor k=5; neighbour k=10)
entry_exit_fill_rules.exit_fill: close(D1+k); the time exit is issued at the immediately preceding decision instant (D1+k-1) so the exit fill is also never same-bar
entry_exit_fill_rules.overlap_policy: max one open position per pair; a new event on a pair with an open position is skipped and counted collision_skipped (no stacking, no early exit, no re-entry); with monthly/quarterly clock cadence vs k <= 10 this is expected never to bind in S0, and it is frozen so it cannot bind asymmetrically across arms
entry_exit_fill_rules.skip_accounting: every skipped event carries a reason code and the clock tuple; trades + skips must reconcile to the published per-economy clock counts or the run is BLOCKED

costs.tier_2_0: PRIMARY GATE: anchor mean per-trade net bps must be > 0 at 2.0x (6.0 bps round trip) for any survival claim
costs.break_even_reporting: per-side break-even = |mean gross per-trade bps| / 2, reported against the 1.5 bps floor (P-2 margin convention)

dual_books.costed: net of ladder costs + financing per the inherited accounting kernel formula (kernel-owned, no new financing assumptions)
dual_books.invariant: sign(price_only mean) must equal sign(costed mean); any inversion is an accounting HARD_FAIL, never a rescue

cells.definition: 3 arms x 2 books = 6 cells (max six cells respected); the cost ladder is a stress recomputation of the costed book, not additional cells

arms.rule: own-economy clock events, direction sign(R), enter close(D1), hold k=5 decision sessions, time exit close(D6)
identical to anchor except k=10 (hold horizon is the single differing design axis); supports the anchor by testing whether measured drift, if any, is first-week continuation or persists a second week

identical rule to the anchor with every published clock's conditionable date shifted +7 calendar days (same weekday by construction; CA boundary rows shift from their available_for_daily_decision_date); the sham's D_prev is the previous weekday of the shifted date; same price series, same fills, same costs, same evidenced semantics, same fold contract
arms.coincidence_note: a shifted date coinciding with a real published clock is mechanically reported and does NOT alter the sham (the sham is defined by the shifted calendar, not by release absence; no discretion)

falsification_rule.identifying_metric: mean per-trade NET PnL in bps at 1.0x ladder on the pooled arm population (computed identically for sham and anchor)
falsification_rule.family_dead_condition: if sign(sham identifying metric) == sign(anchor identifying metric) AND |sham| >= 0.5 * |anchor| -> the family is DEAD: the rule earns regardless of which calendar it is conditioned on, i.e. it is generic short-horizon momentum wearing calendar language (the V5-measured sham shadow from the opposite side); no rescue, no reinterpretation
falsification_rule.reject_condition: anchor identifying metric <= 0 at 1.0x -> REJECT (no post-release drift survives costs at the frozen floor)
survival_requires: sham does NOT reproduce anchor (not same-sign at >= 0.5x magnitude)
anchor net mean > 0 at 2.0x tier (PRIMARY gate)

fold non-vacuity: >= 30 pooled anchor trades in EACH of the 3 folds (measured clock populations give 90/78/78 pre-skip, so this gate can only fail on implementation data-mapping failure - reported margin per P-2)
drop-one fold robustness: pooled mean of each 2-fold subset shares the full-sample anchor sign (with purge, below)

drop-top-pair sign robustness (USD-concentration gate): excluding the single largest net contributor pair keeps the identifying metric same-sign; per-pair and USD-base-vs-USD-quote splits reported as usd_drift_diag

sanity gate EVENT_REACTION_NONDEGENERACY: median |R| on clock-event days must exceed median |R| on non-clock decision days of the same pairs over S0; if violated the direction signal is not event-anchored and the family is DEAD regardless of PnL
sanity gate CA_BOUNDARY_COUNT: exactly 3 CA events may use next-weekday conditionability; any other count is an implementation BUG -> BLOCKED, never silently absorbed
falsification_rule.purge: drop-one computations purge trades whose hold spans a fold boundary (purge_days = 16 calendar days, covering max hold 11 sessions); per-fold stats assign by event decision_date D0
falsification_rule.sham_must_run: the sham MUST produce trades (same shifted clock count per fold as the anchor); a sham that cannot run is a design failure (plan section 4 D2), reported BLOCKED, never 'control not applicable'

expected_failure_interpretation.reject_with_flat_or_negative_sham: the daily decision close fully impounds the print at this granularity: no tradable post-announcement drift after 3.0 bps round trip. Scientifically: semi-strong efficiency at the daily clock for CPI prints in this universe/window; any drift that exists dies inside the first post-availability day (intraday), which daily snapshots CANNOT test - recorded as an information-limitation result, not as calendar-evidence failure
expected_failure_interpretation.sham_reproduces: the mechanism was momentum dressed as release conditioning; placebo falsification fires and the family joins the measured shadow inventory
expected_failure_interpretation.anchor_negative: post-print REVERSAL (overreaction), not drift: informative about direction for any future preregistration, still a REJECT for this family
expected_failure_interpretation.tier_2_0_fail_with_positive_gross: drift exists but is thinner than 6 bps round trip: real but non-tradable at the frozen cost floor; recorded, no rescue

fold_contract.drop_one: 3 drop-one subsets; each remaining-pair pooled mean must share the full-sample anchor sign; fold boundaries and the purge rule above are frozen now
fold_contract.no_fold_may_be_empty: guaranteed by construction (pooled 90/78/78 measured from published clocks) and gated at >= 30 per fold

per_clock_evidence_citation_requirement: every conditioning decision in any artifact of this proposal (each trade, each skip, each fold count) must carry the resolved clock tuple (economy, decision_date, available_time_utc, archive_sha256) byte-resolvable to a row of p3_conditioning_clocks_v6.json; a trade whose tuple cannot be resolved is an invented clock -> HARD_FAIL; per-economy count reconciliation (trades + skips == published clocks in S0: GB 88 / CA 105 / AU 23 / NZ 30) is a mandatory reported check; the 3 CA boundary rows are citable only at their published available_for_daily_decision_date stamps (21:03Z/22:04Z/22:56Z TRUE-UTC, P0b v3)

open_feasibility_questions_for_A9: PRINT VALUES: no CPI print VALUES are archived in the repo (p0a_cpi_prints_ca_v3.json and the GB/AU/NZ calendar pins carry release timing only), and no consensus estimates exist in-repo; the true surprise direction (actual vs consensus, or actual vs prior print) is therefore NOT in-repo computable.
